sources.says: N52: drain plug is behind a small removable access panel on the underside; panel shape and fasteners differ by poster (a triangular panel; three screws); plug orientation reports differ (straight down vs facing right).

E90/E91/E92/E93 DIY: the drain bolt is behind an access hatch just behind the front-centre jack point, opened with a coin; 17 mm socket on a ratchet; copper crush washer replaced each time; the pan is placed a few inches to the right of the bolt.
17 mm plug with copper crush washer; oil exits sideways.

prompt:
Create ONE clean, polished, instructional illustration for a DIY car-repair guide. Text-only prompt: do not use, request or trace any reference image.

SUBJECT: Oil drain: this is the engine oil drain plug, on a 2010 BMW 328i (E90) with the 3.0L inline-6, shown so a home mechanic can see what the step is about. Step: "Drain the sump".

FRAMING: Landscape, exactly 16:10 (deliver 1600x1000 px or larger at 16:10). End-on view straight along the axis of the part, against a plain simplified surface; no ground, horizon or body edges visible. IDENTIFY image: tight close-up of the hero part filling roughly 40-60% of the frame on a plain simplified surface. If an element's orientation is listed as not established, view it end-on with no ground, horizon, body edge or gravity cue. Style (CG-VS-1.0): clean, realistic 3D technical illustration; light neutral studio background (soft white to light grey); matte materials, soft light, soft contact shadows; tight component framing; minimal unnecessary detail. Realism applies to materials and lighting only: it does NOT license invented detail, so every part not listed below stays a plain generic shape. No orange or other saturated accent colours anywhere (a copper-coloured part may be copper); highlights and arrows are added later as an editable overlay.

MUST SHOW (clearly, in this order of importance):
1. HERO: The engine oil drain plug seen end-on: a short plain external hex head (17 mm size) with a flat copper-coloured crush washer under the head. Do NOT depict its orientation: keep it a plain generic shape.
2. A thin flat copper-coloured crush washer sitting between the plug head and the oil pan surface.

MAY SHOW, SIMPLIFIED AND DIM (background only): oil pan surface. Keep every one of these generic and low-contrast. Never invent detail on them.

MUST NOT SHOW (leave these out entirely, do not substitute): pan bolts and ribs (Pan fasteners and rib layout are not established for the automatic pan; left out), wrench or socket, hands, people, engine badges, logos, brand marks, licence plates.

NO TEXT of any kind: no labels, letters, numbers, markings on tools, arrows, callout lines, highlight outlines, banners, watermarks or captions anywhere in the image.

CLEAR SPACE: keep one horizontal band plain and uncluttered (light neutral background only): the top 3%-17% of the height, across the full width. The step banner and labels are added later in software.

Do not add any part not listed above. If unsure how a real part looks, draw a plain generic shape or leave it out.
